diagrams.recognition_to_teach: Horizontal taut string of length 1.2 m attached to vibrating pin of a vibration generator at P and fixed to a vertical wall at Q.
diagrams.source_credit: Cambridge International AS & A Level Physics 9702/21/M/J/24 Question 5 Fig. 5.1

diagrams.recognition_to_teach: Instantaneous displaced sinusoidal wave profile on string contrasted with dashed horizontal equilibrium axis.
diagrams.source_credit: Cambridge International AS & A Level Physics 9702/21/M/J/24 Question 5 Fig. 5.2

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Supplies authentic experimental apparatus context of a taut horizontal string driven by an oscillating vibration generator, illustrating continuous wave train generation and spatial profile vs equilibrium axis.
question_parts_inspected.lesson_relevant_demand: Recognize continuous wave generation on a string driven by a vibration generator and interpret string displacement from equilibrium.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Students frequently fail to recognize that the dashed horizontal line represents the equilibrium position of the unperturbed medium.
lesson_sections_informed: Single pulses and continuous periodic wave trains

diagrams.recognition_to_teach: Horizontal string stretched between fixed ends with node positions indicated by dots, showing point P moving downwards through equilibrium.
diagrams.source_credit: Cambridge International AS & A Level Physics 9702/21/M/J/22 Question 5 Fig. 5.1

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Shows particle P on a string moving downwards through equilibrium, providing authentic evidence that particles oscillate locally across equilibrium while the wave travels.
question_parts_inspected.lesson_relevant_demand: Understand that particles of the medium move through their equilibrium positions with non-zero, changing velocities during wave motion.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Students wrongly assume that a straight string at an instant means particles are at rest.
lesson_sections_informed: Two-track wave analysis: disturbance speed versus particle speed

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Demands stating difference between stationary and progressive wave regarding energy transfer; awards B1 for progressive wave transfers energy / stationary wave does not.
question_parts_inspected.lesson_relevant_demand: Differentiate progressive waves from stationary waves using energy transfer.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Believing all waves carry energy from place to place, neglecting standing wave trapping.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Identifies universal property of all progressive waves: energy is transferred from one position to another with no net transfer of matter.
question_parts_inspected.lesson_relevant_demand: Recognize that progressive waves transfer energy without net matter transport.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Distractor claiming only mechanical waves are progressive, or that progressive waves require atoms.
lesson_sections_informed: Mechanical waves and waves in a vacuum
